question: Should production_start_year and production_end_year use the main OEM generation years or the earliest/latest years across every included body style?
recommended_default: Use European generation umbrella years in v1. Resolve actual fitment with body_code, facelift, and build_date.
why_confirmation_matters: Hatchback, estate, and cabriolet production can differ by one to four years within the same generation. An inconsistent rule creates overlapping or misleading searches.

question: Should facelifts such as B5.5, B8.5, Golf 7.5, and Focus Mk2 facelift be stored as generations or in a separate facelift field?
recommended_default: Keep the OEM generation and add facelift_code/start_year. Only Passat B5 3B to 3BG is provisionally split for operations.
why_confirmation_matters: Lights, exterior panels, interior parts, and electronics often change at facelift, but treating every facelift as a new generation breaks OEM taxonomy.
who_should_confirm: Bulgarian automotive domain expert + at least two dismantlers

question: Do Bulgarian sellers normally present Passat B5 3B and B5.5/3BG as two searchable generations?
recommended_default: Separate them in buyer-facing search while retaining OEM_parent_generation=B5 in the database.
why_confirmation_matters: Volkswagen treats 1996-2005 as B5, but pre- and post-facelift exterior and several part families differ enough to affect dismantler searches.

question: Should the Bulgarian catalogue display Fiesta Mk5/Mk6/Mk7 European numbering or primarily use years and development codes B256/B299/B479?
recommended_default: Display year range plus European Mk name; use B256/B299/B479 as the stable database identifier.
why_confirmation_matters: UK and US references may number the same Fiesta generation differently, which can lead to seller selection errors.

question: When W166 changed from M-Class to GLE in 2015, should the buyer-facing catalogue use one generation with aliases or two records?
recommended_default: Use one generation_id with M-Class, ML, and GLE aliases; store facelift separately.
why_confirmation_matters: The chassis lineage is shared, but the rename coincided with a facelift. Two records duplicate inventory, while a blind merge can misfit exterior parts.

question: Should Civic VIII/IX European hatchbacks FK/FN and sedans FD/FA/FB remain permanently separated as generation variants?
recommended_default: Keep them separate. Share only the model_group and never recommend parts across variants automatically.
why_confirmation_matters: These are different body families under the same generation name, with major differences in panels, glass, interior, and mechanical parts.

question: Do Bulgarian sellers colloquially classify E150/E180 Auris hatchbacks as Corolla?
recommended_default: Do not merge them. Create Auris as a separate model_group and keep Corolla X/XI limited to sedan scope in this version.
why_confirmation_matters: In Europe, Corolla sedan and Auris hatchback are different named body families. Merging them would create many false part matches.

question: Does the local market call 1T1/1T2 and 1T3 Touran I and Touran II?
recommended_default: Keep the OEM first-generation 1T in the database. A buyer-facing Touran II alias may point to 1T3, but must not create a false OEM generation.
why_confirmation_matters: Local parts-catalogue naming can differ from Volkswagen's official generation structure.

question: Does the v1 data model include body_style/body_code, facelift, engine_code, gearbox_code, drivetrain, LHD/RHD, and OE_part_number?
recommended_default: Use generation only as a navigation layer. Compatibility should require OE number plus body/facelift and relevant engine, gearbox, or drivetrain attributes.
why_confirmation_matters: A shared generation does not mean all parts fit. Missing these attributes would incorrectly turn the catalogue into a fitment rule.

question: Can at least two dismantlers provide the last 12 months of donor count, active-part count, enquiries, and completed sales to validate P0/P1/P2?
recommended_default: Use the current priority initially, then rerank using completed sales 40%, enquiries 30%, active parts 20%, and donor vehicles 10%.
why_confirmation_matters: Public registration volume represents potential demand but not dismantler supply depth or actual parts sales velocity.
who_should_confirm: Bulgarian automotive domain expert + partner dismantlers

question: Which of Dacia, SEAT, Hyundai, Kia, Volvo, and Mazda has enough partner-yard inventory to replace lower-priority v1 entries?
recommended_default: Do not add them without evidence. If any make ranks in the partner network's top 14 by donor or sales count, replace low-priority entries such as Fiat Doblo I, Honda Civic VII, or Micra IV.
why_confirmation_matters: The v1 brief limits make coverage to 10-20. Public market statistics do not reveal the inventory mix of the actual dismantler network.
who_should_confirm: Bulgarian automotive domain expert + partner dismantlers

question: Will the marketplace accept UK right-hand-drive donor vehicles, and which part categories must be blocked from automatic left-hand-drive matching?
recommended_default: Allow RHD donors, but apply handedness restrictions to steering, dashboard, pedals, wipers, lighting, and similar parts. Default buyer search to LHD.
why_confirmation_matters: Some Bulgarian donor vehicles may come from the UK. Steering side affects interior, steering, wiper, and lighting components.
